lastText: File ClosedLogistics Did the RestMinor VictoryAllied Combined Chiefs, 1940 — 1945End of hostilities: NOVEMBER 1945 (PROJECTED) — filed out of sequence, pages missingImmediate AftermathVictory in Europe arrives around November 1945 — slower than the historical May 1945, the price of caution at the moments this campaign offered a faster, riskier road instead. The campaign's human cost lands close to the historical one on the Western front — lighter, by a wide margin, than the war the Soviet Union fought over the same years. The Dieppe raid was cancelled — a division of mostly Canadian troops spared its historical destruction, and the opposed-landing lessons that shaped Overlord's doctrine left to be learned later, more slowly, and possibly on the invasion beaches themselves. The Scheldt was cleared before the autumn's offensives rather than after — Antwerp opened weeks early, and the priority error most postwar assessments rank among the campaign's costliest was simply not made. The earliest possible cross-Channel invasion was attempted rather than deferred to Torch — the boldest and most contested strategic choice available to Western Allied command in the entire war. Germany's defeat was never a variable Western Allied command decisions controlled, only its timing, its cost, and the shape of the peace that followed it.One Year LaterA year past victory in Europe, the machinery of occupation is running on the arrangements this campaign's own conferences — Tehran, Yalta, the one
